subject: Bluehaven: narrow log-retention exception for forensic analysis
body:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluehaven.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Day <marcus.day@bluehaven.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: narrow retention exception for tenant debug logs

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — Bluehaven is requesting a temporary, scoped exception to Redwood's default 30-day ephemeral debug-log retention for a single production tenant (tenant id: BH-1138). Our security team is investigating an incident that requires preserving a small subset of request/response debug logs (estimated ~2GB/day) for an additional 90 days beyond the standard window.

Controls we're proposing:
- Restrict retention to BH-1138 only (no other tenants).
- Encrypt retained logs with a customer-specific KMS key (we can provide key material policy).
- Access restricted to Bluehaven SOC+Redwood forensics engineers, with MFA and just-in-time access.
- Read-only export in CSV/JSON delivered via secure share; no long-term replication.

Attached is a small sample extract and our SIG rubric note. Please confirm what evidence Redwood needs (SOC 2 control mapping, CAIQ references, or additional compensating controls) to approve this limited exception.

Best,
Elena Soto
Director, Information Security
Bluehaven Biotech

---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluehaven.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: narrow retention exception for tenant debug logs

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the sample. Looping in Jonas (for forensics/engineering) and Ben (compliance). A few clarifying Qs so we can scope an approval: 

1) Exact retention window request: 90 days from when? From 2025-07-01 or from approval date?
2) Can you confirm the selectors/filters you expect (e.g., request_ids, tenant tag, specific endpoints)? We need to avoid any cross-tenant leakage.
3) Who will own the JIT access approvals on your side? We will mirror an approval workflow but need named approvers.

Ben — from a SOC 2 / SIG perspective, we'll need documented justification, mapping to the relevant CC controls, and evidence of the proposed KMS usage. If Bluehaven wants us to hold data encrypted under their key, we need a KMS integration statement and an ephemeral access policy.

Jonas — can infra put a scoped retention hold for a single tenant and route retained data to a quarantined blob store with the Keystore tag? Estimate we'll need an engineering task and a signed exception.

Elena — attaching the minimal evidence checklist we typically ask for (SOC 2 mapping, CAIQ pointers, list of named approvers). If you can return the signed exception form we can expedite.

Thanks,
Irene
Principal Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-evidence-checklist.txt (stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluehaven.com>, Marcus Day <marcus.day@bluehaven.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: narrow retention exception for tenant debug logs

Irene / Ben — quick engineering note on feasibility and risk:

- We can implement a tenant-scoped retention override as a short-lived exception (config flag + policy layer) and route the logs to a quarantined S3 bucket with object-level ACLs.
- Cost: approx 2GB/day * 90 days ~= 180GB, negligible on infra but we will need to tag and apply lifecycle to ensure deletion after the window.
- We cannot (today) encrypt objects with an external customer-managed KMS key in our multi-tenant blob; we can either:
  a) Hold encrypted payloads uploaded by Bluehaven (they encrypt before upload), or
  b) Use Redwood-managed KMS but restrict key access to a named Redwood service account and log all decrypt operations for attestation.

Recommended path: option (b) with enhanced audit/tracing + signed attestation that we will delete objects after the window and provide Bluehaven a one-time export. If Bluehaven insists on BYOK, we'll need an enterprise private deployment contract amendment.

I can spin up a guarded PoC bucket and policy today if Irene approves a scoped exception.

— Jonas
Engineering Lead, Forensics

---

From: Marcus Day <marcus.day@bluehaven.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: narrow retention exception for tenant debug logs

Thanks — Bluehaven is comfortable with Redwood-managed KMS provided we receive:
- Monthly decrypt logs for the retained objects (audit export).
- A signed attestation at delete time with object manifest.
- Named approvers: Elena Soto (elena.soto@bluehaven.com) and Marcus Day (marcus.day@bluehaven.com).

If you can confirm those controls and provide the small attestation template, we'll sign the exception form and provide the filtered selectors this afternoon.

Marcus
Head of Security Operations
Bluehaven Biotech
